options.content:
Metric names here match what `labs/worker` actually emits, verified against the endpoint. Two things to know before editing a query:

- **Counters have no `_total`** — `temporal_workflow_completed`, not `..._total`. The OpenMetrics convention says otherwise and so does much of the internet, but Temporalio 1.17 does not add it, and `HasCounterTotalSuffix` makes no difference either way.
- **Histograms end `_seconds_bucket`** only because the starter sets `HasUnitSuffix` and `UseSecondsForDuration`; the .NET defaults give you unsuffixed integer milliseconds.
- **Gauges never take a suffix**: `temporal_num_pollers`.

A wrong name returns an empty graph with no error. `curl -s localhost:9464/metrics | grep -E '^temporal_' | cut -d'{' -f1 | sort -u`

panels.title: Workflow task schedule-to-start p99 — is work waiting for workers?
panels.description: The queue, not the work. This is the best 'do I need more workers' signal, and it is your side of the boundary rather than Temporal's.

panels.title: Sticky cache hit rate — is replay being avoided?
panels.description: A falling hit rate means workflows are being evicted and replayed from history, which costs latency and CPU for no functional change.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(temporal_sticky_cache_hit[5m])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(rate(temporal_sticky_cache_hit[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(temporal_sticky_cache_miss[5m])) or vector(0)), 0.001)

panels.title: Task slots available — is the worker saturated?
panels.description: A gauge, so NO _total suffix. Slots pinned at zero means the worker is the bottleneck; slots always full means you sized it larger than you need.

panels.title: Outcomes — completed vs failed vs task failures
panels.description: temporal_workflow_task_execution_failed is the one that catches non-determinism. It climbs while the workflow is stuck but neither completed nor failed, which is why error-rate alerts miss it. The `or vector(0)` is not decoration: a counter that has never fired emits no series at all, so without it the whole panel goes blank the moment nothing is failing — which is exactly when you are looking at it.

panels.title: Pollers (gauge — no _total)
panels.description: Zero pollers means nothing is picking up work. First thing to check when someone says 'Temporal is broken'.
